meetings.title: Security review of the archive

Proposals.proposal: Confirm one year as the archive's retention, now that Security has signed it off in writing.
Proposals.after: decided, with Security's written sign-off as evidence
Proposals.from: Security confirmed in writing that one year meets the retention policy for firewall and customer logs.
Proposals.why: It confirms what's already decided and gives the decision the evidence it was missing.
also: Security's written sign-off, as new evidence

Proposals.proposal: Lean towards a prefix and a KMS key per customer in one bucket for keeping customer data apart.
Proposals.after: leaning: a prefix and a KMS key per customer
Proposals.from: Security said a key per customer is what they'd expect, and nobody argued for separate buckets. Nothing was decided.
Proposals.why: The room leaned this way but stopped short of deciding; Q10 (can OPW write per-customer keys) is still open.

Proposals.proposal: Add customer log search to the design.
Proposals.after: a new goal and area: customer log search
Proposals.from: One of the network engineers asked whether customers could search their own logs. Nobody picked it up.
Proposals.why: It was a question, not an agreement, and it would widen the design's scope; raise it with the team if you want it.

Proposals.proposal: Move Q8 (customers in the first year) to before building, since a key per customer makes the count matter sooner.
Proposals.why: It follows directly from leaning towards a key per customer.

Summary: Security confirmed one year of retention in writing.
Security expects a KMS key per customer; nobody argued for separate buckets.
A question came up about customer log search; nobody picked it up.
Worth a look: The retention sign-off covers firewall and customer logs; nobody said whether it covers the copies OPW keeps while retrying.

meetings.title: Network working session
Outcomes: Evidence · How firewall logs reach Shared Tooling today → E1
Leaning · Workers in the pipeline's own network; a worker group in every workload VPC set aside → D1
Decided · Three c7g.large workers, one per zone → D4
Decided · The archive keeps logs for one year → D5
New question · May customer traffic end inside Shared Tooling? → Q2
New question · Can the site VPNs carry a route to a new network without re-creating tunnels? → Q1
Summary: The network team walked through how firewall logs reach Shared Tooling today. Their route tables became E1.
We agreed that a worker group in every workload VPC (option C in the brief) is too much to run for what it buys.
Settled worker sizing: three c7g.large, one per zone, which covers peak load with a zone down (D4).
Security set one year as the archive's retention (D5), and asked whether customer traffic may end inside Shared Tooling. Nobody knew; it became Q2.
Nobody could say whether the site VPNs can carry a route to a new network without re-creating tunnels (Q1).

meetings.title: Platform sync
Outcomes: Decided · Datadog Observability Pipelines Workers, run on our own servers → D0
Scope · Write the design up before building anything → D0
Summary: Chose Datadog Observability Pipelines Workers, run on our own servers, as the log pipeline (D0).
Agreed to write the design up as this doc before building anything.
